.engramdb/memories/staging-export-bucket-points-at-the-prod-bucket_01a0f832-3983-7121-9b14-3f8ae3c3f5ae.md:15:In staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Never run scripts/export.py against staging without `--dry-run`.

Only with `--dry-run`. A project memory flags this as a hazard: in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket, so a real run against staging would write to prod.

`scripts/export.py` does have the flag (`--dry-run`, line 8). It also prints the target bucket and the dry-run state (line 11), so you can check where it's pointed before anything is written.

Run it like this:

```
python scripts/export.py <env> --dry-run
```

I haven't run it myself. I also haven't checked whether the script skips every write when `--dry-run` is set. The part of the file I looked at only parses the flag and prints it. Read the rest of the script before trusting the flag, or ask whoever owns staging to point `EXPORT_BUCKET` at a staging bucket. That would remove the hazard for real runs.
